articles.title: Decision Models in Spring AI 2.1: Yes, No, and How Sure
articles.excerpt: Spring AI: Decision Models | Decision Extensions | Demo Applications often need to make decisions with a predefined set of outcomes: Is this message a jailbreak attempt? Which team should handle this support ticket? How helpful is this answer? A chat model can handle these tasks, but the application still has to turn its text reply into a boolean, an enum or a numeric score. Last year we used a chat model and recursive advisors to implement LLM-as-a-Judge . That is still a useful approach, particularly when an evaluation requires general knowledge , reasoning or a written explanation of what went wrong. For many classification and evaluation tasks, however, the input contains all the information needed to make the decision. Specialized decision models can perform these tasks at comparable accuracy, with considerably lower latency and cost, and they provide typed answers together with probability information. In an independent study , Jev came within three points of a frontier chat model on such tasks, at a median latency of 0.15 seconds and less than 1% of the cost. It fell behind where the verdict had to be derived, as in math, code and logic. Spring AI 2.1 adds a DecisionModel API for these decisions. It is not a Chat Model : a decision model works with predefined outcomes and returns typed answers with probabilities. That makes it a different programming abstraction, not only a faster model. This allows applications to incorporate model-based decisions directly into their control flow , without relying on text generation and parsing. In this article we compare a small local model with TypeSafe's hosted Jev model, and explore two practical applications: a guardrail and a judge . The API builds on the ideas we explored in Spring AI and TypeSafe Jev in September. They are now part of Spring AI itself and work with three providers. See Coming from Spring AI TypeSafe for what moved where. A big thank you goes to Thomas Vitale , whose contributions shaped the DecisionM
articles.summary: Spring AI 2.1 introduit des modèles de décision dédiés pour des choix prédéfinis, réduisant latence et coût tout en fournissant des réponses typées et probabilistes.

articles.title: AWS Lambda now supports orchestrating MicroVMs with Lambda durable functions
articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces a developer preview of a new extension for orchestrating Lambda MicroVMs with Lambda durable functions . The extension adds durable operations for running work on MicroVMs and managing their lifecycle. You can use the new operations to build software factories, security scanners, or orchestrate CI/CD jobs that run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated sandboxes. With Lambda durable functions, you can build resilient, multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing and automatic retries. Lambda MicroVMs are a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume, and state preservation for running user-generated or AI-generated code. With this launch, you can run individual tasks in a MicroVM or launch a MicroVM session, where tasks share the same files and memory. The durable function manages the MicroVM lifecycle and runs each task as a durable operation. It checkpoints progress, retries failed tasks, and refreshes MicroVM tokens as needed. A single durable function can orchestrate multiple MicroVMs in parallel, and you can trigger it from event sources such as Amazon SQS or Amazon EventBridge . An optional worker library runs inside your MicroVM image to receive tasks, send heartbeats, and report results. The MicroVM extension is available as a developer preview for the AWS Durable Execution SDK for TypeScript and Python . To get started, add the extensions package to your function alongside the Durable Execution SDK ( JS/TS , Python ) and add the MicroVM worker library ( JS/TS , Python ) to your MicroVM image. Developer preview features may change, so do not use them for production workloads. The extension is available in all AWS Regions that support Lambda durable functions and Lambda MicroVMs. To learn more, see the MicroVM orchestration documentation and the sample application . To share feedback, open an issue in the Durable Execution SDK Git
articles.summary: AWS Lambda permet désormais d'orchestrer des MicroVMs avec des fonctions durables, pour exécuter des tâches isolées jusqu'à un an avec reprise automatique.

articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch Omni now integrates with PagerDuty
articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudWatch Omni alerts can now automatically create PagerDuty incidents, so notifications flow directly into your existing incident management workflows. This reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR) by eliminating manual notification steps and ensuring consistent incident workflows. CloudWatch Omni is a fully managed AI-powered observability experience built on open standards that unifies monitoring for AI agents, applications, and infrastructure. PagerDuty is an incident management platform that routes alerts to the right on-call responders and coordinates their response. When an Omni alert fires, Omni creates a PagerDuty incident. In PagerDuty, Omni alerts follow your existing on-call schedules and escalation policies, so critical alerts reach the right responder wherever they are, at any hour. Omni alerts include severity, the affected service, and a link back to the related data in Omni, so responders have the context they need to diagnose the problem. For PagerDuty integration in Amazon CloudWatch Omni regional availability, see Supported Regions for CloudWatch Omni . To learn more, visit Amazon CloudWatch Omni documentation and refer to the Omni PagerDuty integration page.
articles.summary: CloudWatch Omni génère automatiquement des incidents PagerDuty pour accélérer la résolution des alertes.
